newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Western, domestic buying pushes up Russian shares. [CORRECTED 13:57 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Western, domestic buying pushes up Russian shares. [CORRECTED 13:57 GMT]

text.p: Leading Russian shares continued their New Year rally on Friday, with many stocks hitting new record highs, dealers said.

"Demand is coming from two directions: there is real demand from Western investors while domestic participants are covering short positions," said Pavel Gronbjerg (corrects from Gryunberg), co-head of equities at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell.
"But the demand is there. This is a rally."
Dealers said even the most liquid shares, known locally as the blue chips, were extremely volatile, with prices moving within ranges between three and 20 percent above Thursday's close.
The market has ignored news about the health of President Boris Yeltsin, admitted to hospital on Wednesday with pneumonia.
At 1250 GMT Mosenergo, a proxy for the whole market for many foreign investors, was at $1.45, off an earlier $1.50 high, after closing on Thursday at $1.26. At Christmas it was below $1.00.
Irkutskenergo was at a record $0.215, after closing at $0.170. It rose sharply in the afternoon after confirming plans to issue ADRs later this month.
Surgutneftegaz, whose own ADR issue is due to start trading any day now, was $0.630 after closing at $0.575.
Dealers said there was still no sign of a correction after the rapid gains, even though one was expected imminently.
"The most interesting thing is that despite all the forecasts everything is rising furiously," said IK Prospekt dealer Andrei Ippolitov.
"Everyone who could has already sold almost everything but investors are happy to buy at these prices and are even paying a premium."
He forecast demand would soon move to second-tier shares from the blue chips.
